Before Driftwise Meadow was covered in snow, it was a land of clear lakes and vast fields of blue flowers. The Skippies played freely in the water, while the Nimbis drifted quietly through the blooms, steeped in sadness, and releasing melancholic mists that drifted and lingered in the air. Even when ancient Idyllians came here, they would grow sad and weep uncontrollably upon touching those mists. Over time, this gave rise to the legend of the Weeping Lake. But as the fiery power of the Russet Highlands weakened, this land gradually grew cold. The lake froze, snow accumulated, and the Aniimo living here began to change in wondrous ways. Yet the Nimbis remained much as they had been long ago, as though untouched by time—until the arrival of the Fentufts made them so sorrowful that they started shedding melancholic fluff.
This year's abundant sunshine has helped the flowers grow beautifully, so the honey produced should be especially fragrant and sweet.

I spent my twentieth birthday with Tucker.
It was a rare sunny day in the Mistwoods, and we met up at <style=Hint_BgD>our old spot</style>.

...

Our magic sound is more powerful than theirs, hands down!
...
Even the Pomeggs, who love a good bit of noise, ran off.
...
Looking around, there wasn’t a single Hummin left.
...
Sure enough, we made everyone in the Mistwoods hear our singing!
Although no one could tell we were singing the “Birthday Song.”
...
I never used to like singing the birthday song, nor celebrating birthdays.
Because I’ve been off-key since I was little, and everyone always laughed at me.
But singing together with Tucker, even if the whole Mistwoods can’t stand it, I’m happy.
I’m starting to look forward to my next birthday.
The next birthday, and the one after, and the one after that... I want to spend them all with Tucker!

Glynsera and Scorchhowl are both born for battle. Each leads its own kind in the fight for Beast Fang Ridge, and even Boneskies and Emberpups cannot stay out of it. During one battle, a Bonesky tumbled down a hillside and broke its leg. An Emberpup carried it back to safety. The Bonesky couldn’t understand why its enemy had saved it. The Emberpup simply said, "You’re going to be my rival one day. I can’t have you ending up as a crippled wolf, forgotten in some corner." The Emberpup’s honesty and fighting spirit inspired the Bonesky, and the two made a promise: each would become the strongest of their own kind before meeting again for a final duel. Determined to become the strongest on Beast Fang Ridge, they each set off to find their own path to strength. You became the witness to that promise. In time, the Bonesky fulfilled that promise and became Recas, the mightiest Glynsera. The leg that had once been broken became the weapon with which it claimed glory. But when the Emberpup never returned to keep its promise, loneliness slowly consumed Recas. It came to realize that the price of strength wasn’t just broken bones and battle scars, but also the cold and loneliness that came with it.
